title: Shino Can't Say Her Name
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Shino Oshima has a speech disorder that makes words starting with vowels, including her own surname, hard to say, and her first day of high school ends in laughter. Classmate Kayo begins talking with her through notes, and the two form a band, with Kayo on guitar and Shino singing. When Kikuchi, the boy who mocked Shino, asks to join, Shino's fragile confidence breaks. A single-volume story by Shuzo Oshimi.
life_message: Friendship and finding your own voice, in music or in words, matter more than appearing normal.

folkways.japan: The ordeal of the self-introduction on the first day of a Japanese school year, and fear of standing out, frame Shino's anxiety.

delivery.evidence: Outer Haven: lessons come through dialogue and Kayo's and Kikuchi's perspectives, not overt statements.
delivery.note: Shino's growth is shown through events, with little moralizing.

winners_losers: Shino and Kayo keep their friendship and Shino begins to find her voice; Kikuchi's redemption is only hinted; sympathy goes to Shino.
